21 states and the District of Columbia have statewide mandatory helmet laws for children. 29 US states have no statewide law, and 13 of these states have no such laws in any lower-level jurisdiction either.
No requirement except for users of electric power-assisted bicycles with more than 250W engine or electric powered speed excess 25 km/h.
Mexico City repealed mandatory helmet laws in 2010.
Article 63-11 of the Road Traffic Act requires that persons responsible for children under 13 must ensure that the children wear helmets. However, there is no penalty associated with this article.
No requirement nationwide, but some cities such as Quezon City have helmet mandate laws, with non-compliance punishable with fines.
Mandatory for children below 12 year old (passenger or driver), fines apply.
Compulsory for all cyclists but in practice the law is not enforced. No fine had been agreed.
Mandatory. Fines are collected by the provinces.

Laws vary by province and territory. Helmets are compulsory in British Columbia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Helmets are mandatory for cyclists under the age of 18 in Alberta, Manitoba, and Ontario. Helmets are not required …
Compulsory for all ages in public spaces except for those older than 17 in the Northern Territory that are not using car carriageways (e.g: footpaths, cycle paths, trails).
Mandatory in urban zones and suggested in rural zones.
No penalty for children cycling alone who do not obey the law. Also applies to Segway use.
Mandatory helmet policy was enacted by the National Assembly of Togo, since 1975 but the enforcement by the National Police only started in Jun 2013 upon enactment of a new road code.
Starting from 2011, only applies under 18 years of age, in interurban ways and during sport events.
Wearing a helmet increases the speed limit for bicycles outside populated areas from 40 km/h to 50 km/h.

In 2009, Transport Secretary announced that government had no intention of introducing mandatory helmet law, based partly on "international views that a mandatory requirement may lead to a reduction in cycling activities."
Since 2018, all cyclists (power-assisted or not) must wear a helmet.
Not required, but recommended.
Only cyclists under 15 years of age (no fines apply).
Mandatory for children below 16 only if riding on a road.
Mandatory for all riders.
Bicycles: Only under 10 year olds riding as passengers on an adult's bicycle are required to wear a helmet.
Iceland has considered – but not pursued – extending its helmet law to adults.
Failure to comply with the Law could result in a fine being issued.
Cyclists "should" wear helmets, but they are not compulsory.
